# Security Checklist: ISK-0007 — Container Entry Points & Process Separation

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for listeners, images, value-free output, telemetry, and supply chain are complete, clear, and traceable to the threat model
**Created**: 2026-11-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Listeners

- [x] CHK001 - Is the separation of the health and traffic listeners defined by a property that a caller cannot choose? [Clarity, Contract §Listeners 2, Research R10]
- [x] CHK002 - Is the health listener's answer to any other path or method defined? [Completeness, Contract §Listeners 3]
- [x] CHK003 - Are the limits of plain HTTP and an unauthenticated health port recorded as accepted, with their owner and later spec? [Assumption, Spec §AV-5, Contract §Known limits, §Left to later specs]

## Images

- [x] CHK004 - Are the runtime user and group given as fixed numbers, so an orchestrator can check non-root? [Measurability, Spec §FR-026, Contract §Images 2]
- [x] CHK005 - Are both base images pinned by digest, with the rule for changing a digest? [Completeness, Spec §FR-026, Contract §Images 1]
- [x] CHK006 - Is the read-only root filesystem requirement complete, including what must be writable for it to hold? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases, Contract §Images 2]
  - Settled in `checklist`: the contract said `/tmp` "should be" a `tmpfs`, which left a read-only root with no writable `/tmp` undefined. It now says that with a read-only root, `/tmp` must be mounted writable, as a `tmpfs` or an empty volume, and T044's operator guide says so.
- [x] CHK007 - Is the image's entry point form specified, so that container arguments reach the command line, and is the health-check form defined for an image with no shell? [Gap, Spec §TR-10, Contract §Images 2]
  - Settled in `checklist`: research R16 and T030 gave `ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "<host>.dll"]` with no working directory, and named no `HEALTHCHECK`. The contract, R16, and T030 now set `WORKDIR /app` and `ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "/app/<host>.dll"]`, declare no `HEALTHCHECK` because the orchestrator chooses its probes (Listeners rule 6), and give the exec-form `health` command.
- [x] CHK008 - Is image content defined negatively, naming what each image must not hold: the other plane, SDK, source, tests, shell, package manager, setuid or setgid files? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, §FR-026, Contract §Entry points 4, §Images 2]
- [x] CHK009 - Is AV-4's licensing validation recorded with its evidence? [Assumption, Spec §AV-4, Research R16]

## Value-free Output

- [x] CHK010 - Is the set of values that must never appear defined the same way for readiness, events, exit diagnostics, and logs? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020, §FR-029, §SC-006, Contract §Readiness 10, §Diagnostics 6]
- [x] CHK011 - Is it specified how ASP.NET Core's own request logs, which hold paths and hosts, are kept out? [Gap, Contract §Telemetry 3, Research R15]
- [x] CHK012 - Is the unexpected-failure diagnostic limited to the exception's type name? [Clarity, Contract §Diagnostics 4]
- [x] CHK013 - Is SC-006's canary measurable: which values are planted and where they are searched for? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006, Tasks T034]

## Telemetry and Supply Chain

- [x] CHK014 - Is the exporter's presence tied to one explicit variable, with nothing exported otherwise? [Clarity, Spec §FR-028, Contract §Telemetry 2]
- [x] CHK015 - Can the telemetry subscription be built within the container library's approved references? [Dependency, Gap, Research R15, Rules contract §Approved references]
  - Settled in `checklist`: R15 and T028 named `PostgreSqlAdapter.DiagnosticsName`, which is in `Iskender.Infrastructure.PostgreSql`, outside the `Iskender.Infrastructure.<Adapter>` pattern's approved references. The persistence contract's Telemetry section fixes the name `Iskender.Persistence`, so R15 and T028 now use it as a literal, with a test that compares it to the constant. No edge is added, so FR-004 and FR-031 hold.
- [x] CHK016 - Are the new packages' licenses recorded with their source, and is AV-2's validation tied to `check-license.sh`? [Assumption, Spec §AV-2, Research R15]
- [x] CHK017 - Is every row of the spec's Negative Security and Failure Scenarios table traced to a contract rule? [Traceability, Spec §Negative Security and Failure Scenarios, Contract §Threat model]
